title: FOMC decision (meeting Jul 27-28, no SEP) — the session after the July 2027 Consumer Confidence print
source: EST: federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm, fetched direct 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200, 164,831 bytes -- byte-identical to the April, May and June siblings' fetches) and parsed out of the page's own 2027 panel, which reads verbatim "January 26-27 | March 16-17* | April 27-28 | June 8-9* | July 27-28 | September 14-15* | October 26-27 | December 7-8*" with the footnote "* Meeting associated with a Summary of Economic Projections." -- so July 27-28 carries NO SEP. Page's own stamp: "Last Update: August 19, 2026". The parse was run with the two traps this chain has banked defeated (a lookahead rather than a consumed trailing delimiter; abbreviated cross-month labels expanded) and with the 06-29 sibling's standing assertion checked before anything downstream was trusted: 8 meetings per year, 56 in total, 17 collisions in the tape window -- all three held. Filed estimate not for want of a primary but because the same page states verbatim "Each meeting date is tentative until confirmed at the meeting immediately preceding it" -- the 2027-06-08/09 meeting is the confirming venue -- and because this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. Statement time assumed 14:00 ET per the standing convention, not separately sourced. Discovered during the consumer-confidence-2027-07-27 initial research, checked 2026-09-06
notes: Proposed during the consumer-confidence-2027-07-27 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-06) because that print's +/-5-day corridor returned EXACTLY ZERO tracked entries -- and so does the whole of July and August 2027, in which this calendar currently holds nothing at all. The nearest tracked event to 2027-07-27 in either direction is consumer-confidence-2027-06-29, twenty-eight days earlier. WHAT THE GAP WAS HIDING IS THE ONE DAY THAT MEASURABLY MATTERS. Re-measured this session on n=1,447 sessions (2020-12-01 -> 2026-09-04, stockanalysis.com bars plus CBOE VIX_History.csv), FOMC DECISION days run 8 of 9 wider than no-Fed sessions -- SPY 1.352 vs 0.958 p=0.0001, XRT p<0.0001, XLY 0.0001, XLF 0.0001, TLT 0.0007, QQQ 0.0011, AMZN 0.0012, AAPL 0.0051, VIX the lone null -- while FOMC DAY ONES are 0 of 9 (SPY 0.929/0.958, p=0.2971), exactly replicating the fomc-2027-04-28 and consumer-confidence-2027-04-27 measurements. The Consumer Confidence print lands on day one, the silent day; the content is here, one session later. Across the six July instances on the tape the decision session ran wider than the print that preceded it in four (SPY range %, print -> decision: 2021 0.898 -> 0.680 narrower, 2022 1.044 -> 2.239, 2023 0.631 -> 0.794, 2024 1.616 -> 1.078 narrower, 2025 0.679 -> 0.966, 2026 0.921 -> 1.835) -- four of six is an illustration at n=6, not a test, and the claim that carries is the n=45 decision-day result above. THIS IS THE COLLISION MONTH, DETERMINISTICALLY: every FOMC day one falling in January, April, July or October is the last Tuesday of that month, 22 of 22 across 2021-2027, which is why a July Consumer Confidence print has never once been observed clean (0 of 6) and why this pairing recurs every year rather than being a 2027 anomaly. SAME CHANNEL CAVEAT AS THE OTHER RATE ENTRIES: symbols is empty and no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is rates- or FX-keyed. Two things for the pulses: confirm the date once the 2027-06-08/09 meeting ratifies the calendar, and note that the minutes for this meeting fall on 2027-08-18 by the Board's own three-week convention (42 of the 45 published minutes dates on that page sit exactly 21 days after their decision day) -- deliberately NOT proposed here, because at D+22 it sits outside this print's corridor and belongs to whichever lane takes this event. Estimate widens caution only; nothing here licenses an entry.
